missions.title: The Paper Landing
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can the order in which we take a reading change what we can carry forward?
missions.stake: If Sora sends the story without its label, the next reader may use a paper landing as a direction.

objectives.title: Try the peg and tide wheel. Press a proof for the Cold Store.

missions.title: Where the Slip Takes You
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When does a useful instruction need the history behind it?
missions.stake: A new caller has little time. An earlier caller still needs a way to check the old return.

objectives.title: Bring the print to Aster and line it up with the practice desk receipts.
Hang the checked directions. See where the reader goes.

items.name: The Paper Landing proof
items.description: A print from Sora’s invented cut-paper tale. The press took the reading made during one pass. The Cold Store’s practice desk has room for it.

dialogue.speaker: sea-harbourkeeper
dialogue.text: Sora’s cut-paper play has a rail on the left and a shelter on the right. In the tale, a landing can follow a voice. A baker once called it by accident and found the whole landing under her flour table. In Sora’s model the tide wheel calls it to the shelter. A peg stays in whichever hole you press it into.

options.text: Unfold the play with its landing by the rail.
Lift the peg. Turn the paper landing back to the rail.
Step back from the practice rail.

dialogue.speaker: sea-harbourkeeper
dialogue.text: On the real harbour chart you left a margin where the survey stopped. The checked strip is still on the chart. This is our made-up landing. The peg is north of the board. The wheel is to the south. See what happens to your mark here.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The model starts again by the rail. Your peg is loose. Sora leaves the paper press open while you try another pass.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The removable peg fits either of the paper board’s two holes. The landing and the hole line up at this moment.

options.text: Push the peg in beside the rail before turning the wheel.
Push the peg in under the shelter where the landing is now.
Leave the peg loose.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The peg holds the first place by the rail. From the shelter, the new arrival still has a wall between their eyes and the peg. The tide wheel is ready.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The peg holds the current place under the shelter. A reader at the shelter can match it to the landing. The hole by the rail stayed empty during this pass.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A paper caller lifts a little hand as you take the wheel. The slot leads across the board from the rail to the shelter. The real chart on Market Rail stays in place.

options.text: Turn the wheel and bring the landing under the shelter.
Turn the wheel while holding your first-place peg still.
Leave the caller’s hand down.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The landing tucks under the shelter by the paper caller. There is still time to put a peg where it is now. The first hole keeps no mark of where it was.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The cutout arrives under the shelter. Your peg stays one position back by the rail. Sora lays your two places along the same turn, with their order marked.

dialogue.speaker: sea-harbourkeeper
dialogue.text: Sora has one pocket for the copy to travel. The press takes an impression from the pass you just played. You can reset the cutouts at the board before making a copy.

options.text: Press a two-place proof with before and after in order.
Press an arrival proof with the place you could mark.
Leave the press open and walk back to the board.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: BEFORE THE TURN: beside the rail. AT THE TURN: under the shelter. The first peg stays at the rail. Sora stamps FICTIONAL PAPER PLAY on the proof. Aster in the Cold Store keeps a separate practice desk for trying ways of passing a record.

dialogue.speaker: preserved-registrar
dialogue.text: Your print saved where the paper landing started. I have a visitor looking for a slot she used last week. Before we point, check the actual practice desk receipts on the short shelf.

options.text: Place the fictional print on the practice desk.
Keep the practice print in my pocket.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: AT MY ARRIVAL: under the shelter. The peg stays where I saw the paper landing. The start of this pass is unmarked. Sora stamps FICTIONAL PAPER PLAY on the proof. Aster in the Cold Store keeps a separate practice desk for trying ways of passing a record.

dialogue.speaker: preserved-registrar
dialogue.text: Your print kept the arrival sighting close to the instruction. There is a late caller coming for a new rehearsal request. Check the dates on the actual practice desk receipts before you make a ticket.

options.text: Place the fictional print on the practice desk.
Keep the practice print in my pocket.

dialogue.speaker: preserved-registrar
dialogue.text: Aster puts a blue cover under the paper play. A plain strip points to the practice receipts. The Cold Store’s collection records have their own cases.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Last week, bell two: Aster signed for completed rehearsal returns at the west rail. Today, bell four: Aster signed to take new rehearsal requests at the east shelf. The current intake line also directs return questions to the registrar.

options.text: Set the actual receipts beside the fiction. Keep the signers, jobs and dates with the directions.
Close the practice folder.

dialogue.speaker: preserved-registrar
dialogue.text: Both actual slips belong to this fictional archive’s practice desk. Their dates and different jobs give Aster something to check before hanging a direction. The paper landing stays with the play.

dialogue.speaker: preserved-registrar
dialogue.text: The old receipt and the current one include different dates and duties. A two-place slip at the former rail would help someone arriving on the old directions. She will have one more line to read.

options.text: Fold the dated slips together for the former collection rail.
Let Aster keep both receipts on the short shelf.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The folded slip has two panels. The former rail and the current shelf have a date, a signature and a different job each.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The folded slip has two panels. The former rail and the current shelf have a date, a signature and a different job each.

options.text: Hook the two dated panels side by side.
Keep the clip empty for now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Aster clears the old clip. The first panel says where rehearsal returns were taken before the move. The second takes callers with new requests to the east shelf.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A visitor comes back to the former rail holding last week’s request. She stops at the date on the left panel. Her own receipt has the same little corner cut.

options.text: Align her receipt with the old date. Let her follow the newer panel.
Give the reader some time.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: She confirms which shift took her return. Aster handles her question. She takes the new request east. Aster keeps both panels and adds a small clip for visitors carrying an old receipt.

dialogue.speaker: preserved-registrar
dialogue.text: A single line at the east shelf would send a late caller straight to new requests. The former rail still has the older receipt for returns. We can give that trip to the keeper if the caller needs it.

options.text: Cut a current-room ticket for the east shelf.
Let Aster keep both receipts on the short shelf.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The short ticket names the current place and job. There is room underneath for one dated footnote.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The short ticket names the current place and job. There is room underneath for one dated footnote.

options.text: Attach the short ticket and clip the earlier receipt reference beneath it.
Keep the clip empty for now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The face of the ticket gives new requests to the east shelf. A small dated tab sends questions about last week’s returns to the keeper.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A late caller checks the job on the front of the ticket. He has a new request in one hand. His companion still has a return slip.

options.text: Slide the request tray towards him. Pull out the earlier receipt reference for his companion.
Give the reader some time.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: He files the new request from the east shelf. His companion takes the referral to the keeper. Aster leaves the pull-out tab in reach for the next pair.

hints.text: The peg and wheel have different jobs on Sora’s model.
Follow what happens to the mark as the cutout crosses. The board can reset a pass.
A peg can stay at the first place. A later peg can give a reader the arrival place.
Use both props, then go to the press at the pocket. Your latest pass sets the copy.
Aster has a practice desk for the print.
The practice receipts have their own shelf. Look for a pair of dated slips.
The former rail and the current shelf have different jobs on the signed slips.
Read the receipt scene east of Aster’s practice desk, then bring the checked slips back.
Aster has a place ready for the checked direction.
The two-place slip goes at the former rail. The compact ticket goes by the current shelf.
Hang the direction, then see which reader stops there.
Open the same rail a second time after fitting the slip. Help the reader use it.

journal.title: The Paper Landing
journal.text: I kept the result of one order from Sora’s fictional paper play. Aster can try its way of marking a place against the practice desk receipts.

journal.title: Where the Slip Takes You
journal.text: I used the archive's own dates and signatures for the directions. I kept the paper story with its own label and helped a reader try the new slip.
